newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth to buy Koenig Sporting Goods stores.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth to buy Koenig Sporting Goods stores.

text.p: Retailer Woolworth Corp said Friday it had agreed to buy stores from bankrupt Koenig Sporting Goods Inc for about $10 million in cash.

Woolworth said in a statement it was buying 27 stores in markets where its Champs Sports division did not have a presence or operated a limited number of stores. The markets include Cleveland, Pittsburgh and Buffalo, it added.
It said it expedcted the acquisition to be accretive to earnings as it converted the stores to its Champs Sports format.
First Call's consensus among analysts forecast a profit of $1.64 per share for fiscal 1998 against $1.26 the previous year.

"There are currently 540 Champs Sports stores located throughout North America, and this acquisition, together with the additional store openings planned, will accelerate the growth of the company," Woolworth said.
Koenig, a privately held sporting goods retailer based out of Cleveland, operates 40 stores in six states.
"Koenig intends to exit the sporting goods business and resolve its financial obligations through a Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceeding," it said.
